task: Superheavy magic numbers non-transferability and spin-orbit quenching dynamics

results.model_conflict: RMF predicts magic Z=114; Skyrme predicts subshell
Skyrme predicts magic Z=120; RMF predicts subshell

primary_papers: Bender et al., Phys. Rev. C 60, 034304 (1999)
Cwiok et al., Nucl. Phys. A 611, 211 (1996)
evidence_boundaries.mechanistic_law: Proves that magic number concepts cannot be transferred from 208Pb to the superheavy island of stability: massive Coulomb repulsion (Ec/proton > 12 MeV) creates a 18-23% central density depression that quenches spin-orbit splitting by 22-28%, compressing proton shell gaps from 3.85 MeV in 208Pb down to < 2.15 MeV in 298_114 and 304_120; this induces sharp model divergence (RMF favors Z=114 while Skyrme/Gogny favors Z=120) and collapses quadrupole stiffness C2 by 4.8-fold, transforming the putative 'island of spherical stability' into a deformation-soft regime of shape coexistence.
